title.narrative: Strengthening Fiscal and Financial Stability Project

description.narrative: The Project Development Objective is to contribute to the Government of Mongolia's efforts to strengthen fiscal and financial stability and improve the quality of expenditure management.

The development objective of Strengthening Fiscal and Financial Stability Project for Mongolia is to contribute to the government of Mongolia's efforts to strengthen fiscal and financial stability and improve the quality of expenditure management. This project has five components. 1) The first component, Strengthening Macroeconomic and Fiscal Management, aims to strengthen fiscal responsibility and support the implementation of relevant policy measures toward (a) improving the quality of expenditure management, (b) strengthening macroeconomic and budget policy-making capacity, and (c) improving regulatory processes. It has the following three subcomponents: (i) Improving macroeconomic policy tools and enhancing research capacity; (ii) Strengthening fiscal policy and planning; and (iii) Strengthening capacity for debt management and external development financing operations. 2) The second component, Improving the Efficiency of Public Financial Management, aims to improve fiscal discipline by strengthening the country's PFM and enhance the quality of expenditures by revamping PIM and fostering activities aimed at increasing transparency and accountability. It has the following four subcomponents: (i) Improving budget credibility, predictability, and execution for better delivery of services; (ii) Increasing budget comprehensiveness and transparency through better control, reporting, and expansion of the recipient's Integrated Financial Management Information System capabilities; (iii) Strengthening the public financial management institutional capacity; and (iv) Strengthening Public Investment Management. 3) The third component, Enhancing Financial Sector Stability, aims to support the MOF, BOM, FRC, DBM, and DICOM to strengthen the resiliency of the banking system. It has the following five subcomponents: (i) Developing and implementing a financial sector development strategy to strengthen financial sector stability; (ii) Providing support to the effective management the Development Bank of Mongolia; (iii) Strengthening financial safety nets; (iv) Strengthening the institutional capacity of the Financial Regulatory Commission; and (v) Improving the capacity of the Bank of Mongolia to enhance financial stability. 4) The fourth component, Strengthening of the Social Protection System, aims is to support the government's efforts to improve public expenditure quality in social protection. It has the following two subcomponents: (i) Strengthening social welfare design, targeting, operations, and performance; and (ii) Strengthening social insurance design, governance, and financial management. 5) The fifth component, Project Management and Monitoring, aims to provide support for project implementation, coordination, monitoring and evaluation, including, among others, audit arrangements, reporting requirements, procurement, and FM activities.

condition.narrative: Section 1, A, 1 (b) The recipient shall establish, and thereafter maintain, throughout the implementation of the Project, theProject Implementation Unit (“PIU”), vested with the responsibility of the overall management and coordination of Project fiduciaryobligations, said PIU to be: (i) headed by the State Secretary of MOF as Project Director, assisted by a qualified and experiencedProject Manager, procurement officer and financial officer, all of whom shall have experience and qualifications acceptable to theAssociation and contracted under terms of reference satisfactory to the Association; and (ii) assigned with such functions, powers,resources and competencies, satisfactory to the Association, as shall be required to achieve its purposes, including the fiduciaryresponsibilities for procurement, financial management, record keeping, disbursement and compliance with monitoring and reportingrequirements.

Section 1, A, 1. (a). The recipient shall establish, and thereafter maintain throughout the implementation of the Project, aninter-ministerial Project Steering Committee, chaired by the Deputy Minister of MOF, and comprised of the representatives of theMOF, MLSP, BOM, and FRC, and assigned with such functions, powers, resources and competencies, satisfactory to the Association, asshall be required for the overall policy guidance and general oversight of Project implementation, including inter-ministerialcoordination, Project monitoring and evaluation, and the liaison with the Association. The Project Steering Committee shall meet atleast once every calendar quarter.

Section I, A, 1 (c) The recipient shall cause each of MOF, MLSP, BOM, DBM, DICOM and FRC to appoint, and thereafter maintainthroughout the implementation of the Project, a coordinator in each of MOF, MLSP, BOM, DBM, DICOM and FRC for the purposes ofhandling the day-to-day technical aspects of the Project activities (other than the fiduciary responsibilities assigned to the PIU)in each of their respective parts of the Project and technical coordination with the PIU, under terms of reference satisfactory tothe Association.

Section II, B. The Recipient shall: (a) not later than January 31, 2020 (or such other date as the Association may agree), carryout a mid-term review of the Project and, prepare and furnish to the Association a mid-term report, in such detail as theAssociation shall reasonably request, documenting progress achieved in the carrying out of the Project during the period precedingthe date of such report, taking into account the monitoring and evaluation activities performed pursuant to paragraph 1 of thisSection II.A, and setting out the measures recommended to ensure the continued efficient carrying out the Project and theachievement of its objective during the period following such date; and (b) review with the Association, such mid-term report, onor about the date one month after its submission, and thereafter take all measures required to ensure the continued efficientimplementation of the Project and the achievement of its objective, based on the conclusions and recommendations of the mid-termreport and the Association's views on the matter.
Section II, C 1. The Recipient shall carry out the Project in accordance with the Project Implementation Manual.

title.narrative: Component B3: Public outreach activities on proposed changes to legislation conducted.

comment.narrative: <p>Formal and informal consultation undertaken in developing new legislation. As examples, in accordance with the Law on Legislation Acts, public outreach activities were undertaken in the process of developing the tax package laws and social welfare laws and engagement was a feature of the work in preparing the package of insurance laws. </p>

title.narrative: Aggregate poverty-targeted social welfare support going to the poorest 20% is increased

comment.narrative: <p>Poverty targeted social welfare increased with the introduction of government payments for health insurance premiums for the poor. Data is impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic (which increased the number of eligible recipients of targeted programs, which subsequently decreased post-COVID-19). In addition, better targeting has reduced the number of citizens who may have been receiving benefits “unfairly” and the government has promoted employment for this cohort – which had the effect of decreasing the spnding on the food stamp program. Nonetheless, the total value of payments targeted to the poorest 20% has increased.</p>

title.narrative: Aggregate deviation of expenditures is reduced to 15% or less and commitment controls are in place.

baseline.value: Aggregate deviation is >15% and no commitment controls in place.

comment.narrative: <p>Average aggregate deviation was less than 4% in each of the last 3 years and on average less than 2%. The score for this corresponding PEFA indicator improved from a sore of D in 2015 to a score of B in 2021.</p>

actual.value: Average aggregate deviation was 1.8% in the three years 2021, 2022 and 2023. Commitments are now recorded in the GFMIS/FBv7 but subject to budget controls only for recurrent expenditure (not capital).

title.narrative: Component B1: The upgraded GFMIS version 7 is operational and customized web services are developed to improve performance, functionality, and integration of the system.

baseline.value: Current version of the GFMIS does not have web services.

comment.narrative: <p>The GFMIS version 7 is operational and configuration/connection with other systems, including the PIMIS, Treasury web-portal, glass account portal and the smart payment system, through web services (Generic Web Services) has been completed.</p>

actual.value: The GFMIS version 7 is operational and configuration and connection with other systems through web services are completed.

title.narrative: Component A1: Fully operational comprehensive revenue forecasting model and financial model for mega-projects.

comment.narrative: <p>Several modelling tools for making projections of the economy and of revenues were implemented, which included a dynamic stochastic general equilibrium (DSGE) econometric model, elements of a fiscal analysis of resource industries (FARI) model as well as a debt, investment, growth and natural resources (DIGNAR) model and the Queensland Pacific Metals (QPM) for commodity price projection, both of which are appropriate for resource-abundant developing countries. As a result, revenue forecasting error decreased. In the case of the FARI model, this was utilized in developing a model for assessing the fiscal impacts of mega-projects, which evolved as a capacity within the broad suite of forecasting tools, rather than as a stand-alone model.</p>

title.narrative: Component D1: Amendments for social insurance legislation in line with the State Policy on Pension Reform (2015-2030) are submitted to the Parliament.

comment.narrative: <p>Social Insurance Package Law was drafted and submitted to the Parliament on October 15, 2021. Social Insurance General Law and Law on Pensions from the Social Insurance Fund and bills were submitted to the Parliament on January 9, 2023. The revised draft social insurance package law was discussed several times in May-July 2023 at the joint session of the SPSC and the Parliament. Four (4) out of the five (5) laws were approved by the Parliament on July 7, 2023, with the draft Law on Private Pension not yet approved.</p>

title.narrative: Component C1: Financial Sector Medium-term Development Strategy: 2017-2025 is prepared and submitted to Parliament.

comment.narrative: <p>Supported by the project, the MOF, BOM, and FRC jointly formulated a “Financial Sector Medium-term Development Strategy: 2017– 2025” national program, which was ratified by the Government (Decree 299) on October 3, 2017. This was further embedded in the legal framework as the Parliament of Mongolia adopted the law on bank recapitalization on June 22, 2018 according to principle that “... oversight and regulatory activities of banking and financial sector will be strengthened, protection of the financial sector customers will be improved”.  Implementation of the strategy was supported by the project, including for example enhancements to trading settlement rules.</p>

title.narrative: Component C5 Operational macro-prudential framework designed and web-based database system operationalized.

comment.narrative: <p>The FRC approved the “Regulation on the establishment and usage of the web-based macroeconomic and financial database” on December 21, 2018. A new unit responsible for macroprudential policy design and implementation has been established within the Monetary Policy Department of the BoM. A range of statistical and economic modelling tools were developed and implemented to suppor this function with the direct support of project consultants, including statistical software, macro forecasting tools including a dynamic stochastic general equilibrium (DSGE) model assessing financial sector stability, and quantitative analysis to support macroprudential policy and risk management – including a financial stability index and stress testing. </p>

title.narrative: Component A2: Government Debt management strategy and action plan are updated and approved by MoF.

comment.narrative: <p>The medium term debt management strategy 2019-2022 was developed with the support of the project and approved by Parliamentary Resolution no. 55 of May 30, 2019. The project also supported the functionality of the debt management system DMFAS, including through translation of the system and its manuals to Mongolian language and training of users.</p>

title.narrative: Component B2: Policy document on budget control and risk management is drafted and approved by MoF.

comment.narrative: <p>Within the framework of the project, the following documents were approved by the MOF (Decree 291, 2019.12.27) in order to introduce risk management policy and practice in accordance with international standards: Risk management policy; Risk Committee charter; and Risk management regulation.</p>

title.narrative: Component B4:The PIM Guideline for regulating the procedures and responsibilities of PIM project strategy/planning, appraisal, selection/prioritization and budgeting developed. and endorsed by MoF.

comment.narrative: <p>To improve the management of public investment planning, the project supported<strong> </strong>enhancements to the methodology for assessing, prioritizing, and selecting public investment projects to be financed by the state budget having regard to sectoral and inter-sectoral priorities as well as economic and financial criteria. This approach was reflected in a Decree No.295 of the Finance Minister on December 25, 2018 and the methodology set out in the regulations. Enhancements were introduced to the Public Investment Management System to support this approach, including a mobile application to support the approved regulation's implementation and rollout and to promote transparency and accountability.</p>

title.narrative: Regulatory framework for the financial sector improved as measured by the number of new or revised legal acts submitted to the Parliament

comment.narrative: <p>The project realized success in enhancing the legal framework for the finance sector, with enhancement to the basic framework for operation of the DBM, FRC, DICOM and BOM. Mongolia’s success in getting off the “grey list” is evidence of the capacity for making amendments to the legal framework improve the operation and oversight of the financial sector.</p>

title.narrative: Component D2: Revised Social Welfare Law draft, which mandates consolidation of the existing social welfare programs, has been submitted to the Parliament for approval

comment.narrative: <p>Many significant amendments were made to the legal framework which, for example, enhanced the sustainability of the age pension. However, the revised draft of the Social Welfare Law, which proposed consolidation of some of the programs and benefits, was submited to the Cabinet in November 2021, is yet to be submitted to Parliament.</p>

title.narrative: Component B1. An Integrated Payroll System (IPS) is developed, tested, and rolled out to strengthen budget control, accountability, and discipline.

comment.narrative: <p>The introduction of an IPS was a major development supported by the project as it automated control over salary payments across government, which represents a significant portion of total expenditure. By September 30, 2023, the system was fully implemented and allowed public sector organizations to calculate the salary of over 186,000 civil servants of 4,358 budget entities and transferred associate funds to the bank accounts of the civil servants through the BoM's interbank transaction system.</p>

actual.value: IPS is developed, fully tested and rolled-out.

title.narrative: Component C3. Digital payout system to deal with different sized banks designed, acquired, and implemented to enhance DICOM effectiveness

comment.narrative: <p>The project supported the acquisition and implementation of a deposit pay out system which collates data and makes analysis of bank deposits to enable swift and efficient payment of deposit insurance when required. At the end of the project the system was procured and installed and ready to operate and was in progress of obtaining access to the deposit data from commercial banks. Further, a deficiency remains regarding the legal framework overall as most commercial banks are withholding data from DICOM on the basis of legislated personal privacy rules. </p>
